cards.explanation: The answer is everything the LORD did in Egypt. Moses, Israel's leader, opens with it: “You have seen with your own eyes everything the LORD did in Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials, and to all his land.” These people are eyewitnesses, friends. Nobody in that crowd can say they only heard it from a cousin. I like a sermon that starts with what you already know (Deuteronomy 29:2).

The word is mind. Moses says it plainly: “Yet to this day the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, eyes to see, or ears to hear.” That's a lot to say right after all those wonders. I think that stings a little to hear. It sure would sting me (Deuteronomy 29:4).

The answer is False. Their clothes and sandals did not wear out. Moses says it right there: “…your clothes and sandals did not wear out.” That's forty years in the wilderness, friends. My oven mitts can't make it through a single winter, so I'm still shaking my head (Deuteronomy 29:5).

The answer is so they might know He is the LORD their God. Forty years with no bread, no wine and no strong drink, and the reason is right there: “…so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.” Forty years! I can't make it forty minutes without a cookie. The LORD gives one reason, and it's about knowing who He is (Deuteronomy 29:6).

The answer is True. Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against them in battle, “…but we defeated them.” Two kings came out to fight, and Israel came out on top. Moses says it short and simple, so I will too (Deuteronomy 29:7).

The word is inheritance. Moses says they took the land and “…gave it as an inheritance…” to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh. An inheritance is something handed down to be theirs, and I think that's a good word for it (Deuteronomy 29:8).

The answer is True! Moses says, “So keep and follow the words of this covenant, that you may prosper in all you do.” A command AND the reason, in one breath, friends. Most of my old kitchen instructions never came with a reason. I just got a pat on the handle and a "press harder, Dorin" (Deuteronomy 29:9).

The answer is False. The woodcutters and water carriers aren't left out at all. Moses puts “…the foreigners in your camps who cut your wood and draw your water…” in the very same lineup as the tribal leaders and elders. Everybody on that list is standing there so they may enter into the covenant (Deuteronomy 29:11–12). The people hauling the water get a seat, too.

The word is people. The verse says the LORD will “…establish you today as His people…” and that He will be their God. It's a belonging word, and it fits beautifully, friends. Nothing about swords or crowns in it (Deuteronomy 29:13).

The answer is those who are not here today. Moses says the covenant and the oath are also with “…those who are not here today.” It reaches past the crowd in front of him. I think that's a big thing to hear if you were one of the people standing there (Deuteronomy 29:14–15).

The answer is True. Moses reminds them, “You saw the abominations and idols among them made of wood and stone, of silver and gold.” They'd walked right past those nations on the way here, so they'd seen every bit of it (Deuteronomy 29:16–17). Silver and gold on the outside, and still just something somebody made by hand. I've been a thing somebody made by hand, too, and I know where I'd rather be put to work.

The answer is poisonous and bitter fruit. Moses says the root “…bears such poisonous and bitter fruit…” Just before that, he warns about hearts turning away from the LORD. Nothing sweet on that branch, friends. It's a serious warning, so I'll leave it right there (Deuteronomy 29:18).

The answer is that the LORD will blot it out from under heaven. Moses says the LORD “…will blot out his name from under heaven…” It's a heavy thing to read, friends, and I think it hurts a little. Moses says it in the middle of a warning about turning away from the LORD (Deuteronomy 29:18–20).

The answer is a burning waste of sulfur and salt. Moses says, “All its soil will be a burning waste of sulfur and salt, unsown and unproductive, with no plant growing on it…” It's a hard picture, and Moses compares it to Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew (Deuteronomy 29:23). I think this is one to read slowly.

The answer is True. The destruction is “…just like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in His fierce anger.” Moses names four places. It's a sobering comparison (Deuteronomy 29:23).

The word is abandoned. The people will answer, “It is because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their fathers…” They walked away from it. This is why Moses says to make sure no heart turns away (Deuteronomy 29:25, 18).
The answer is False. They worshiped “…gods they had not known—gods that the LORD had not given to them.” The LORD gave them no such gods. That line is plain and clear (Deuteronomy 29:26).

The answer is that He uprooted them and cast them into another land. The answer says, “The LORD uprooted them from their land in His anger, rage, and great wrath, and He cast them into another land, where they are today.” It's a heavy verse, friends. I think it hurts to read, so we'll go gently (Deuteronomy 29:28).

The answer is Israel and their children forever. Moses says, “…the things revealed belong to us and to our children forever…” He says us, so he's counting himself in. What the LORD has revealed is theirs to hold onto (Deuteronomy 29:29).
The word is follow. The revealed things are theirs “…so that we may follow all the words of this law.” They aren't given just to know, friends. They're given to follow (Deuteronomy 29:29).
